 IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD  R/SPECIAL CIVIL APPLICATION NO. 435 of 2024  ==================================================
 PRASHANT UDAYAN CHINUBHAI & ORS.
 Versus  PRESIDING OFFICER (LARA) & ORS.
 ==================================================
 Appearance:
 MR. BHASKAR TANNA, SENIOR ADVOCATE WITH MR. DESHAL MODI,
 ADVOCATE WITH MS. SAKSHI SHARMA, ADVOCATE FOR MR NISARG N  TRIVEDI(6144) for the Petitioner(s) No. 1,2,3,4  MS.HETAL PATEL, AGP for the Respondent(s) No. 2,3  ==================================================
 CORAM:HONOURABLE THE CHIEF JUSTICE MRS. JUSTICE  SUNITA AGARWAL  and  HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE PRANAV TRIVEDI  Date : 09/12/2024

sentences.text: ORAL ORDER (PER : HONOURABLE THE CHIEF JUSTICE MRS. JUSTICE SUNITA AGARWAL)
[1] Mr. Deshal Modi, learned advocate has put in appearance to argue the matter though a leave-note has been sent by Mr. Nisarg N. Trivedi.
Prayer to argue is granted.

[2] The petitioners herein seek for quashing of the order dated 10.10.2023 rejecting the application under Section 64 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Prashant Udayan Chinubhai vs Presiding Officer (Lara) on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172343172/
1 Rehabilitation Act, 2013 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act, 2013") dated 09.09.2023, which was filed by the petitioners challenging the award dated 02.05.2015.

entities.label: STATUTE

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The order impugned NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/435/2024 ORDER DATED: 09/12/2024 undefined records that the notice of the award was sent to the petitioners on 01.07.2019 and a reminder notice was sent on 09.10.2019 through R.P.A.D.
Whereafter, the petitioners had submitted an application on 19.12.2019 for disbursement of compensation.
It is, thus, noted that the maximum period of one year six months for making of the application under Section 64 of the Act, 2013 was over by 31.12.2020.

It was, thus,
concluded that the application filed on 09.09.2023 for making reference under Section 64 of the Act, 2013 was delayed beyond 2 years 8 months 9 days and there was no explanation for the same.
[3] By the order dated 19.03.2024, we have granted time to the learned Assistant Government Pleader to file counter affidavit.

Giving para-wise reply to the writ petition, it is stated in the affidavit filed by the Special Land Acquisition Officer, Ahmedabad that after passing of the award dated 02.05.2015, the first notice was sent to the petitioner on 10.07.2019 (wrongly mentioned as 01.07.2019 in the order impugned dated 10.10.2023).
The second notice dated 09.10.2019 was sent through R.P.A.D.

It is also admitted that the petitioners had approached the office of the Special Land Acquisition Officer by making an application on NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/435/2024 ORDER DATED: 09/12/2024 undefined 19.12.2019 for disbursement of the compensation amount.

It seems that nothing was done in the matter and hence, the petitioners had to approach this Court by filing a writ petition, namely, Special Civil Application No.11347 of 2020 with the following prayers:-
"(A) Your Lordship may be pleased to issue a writ of mandamus or any other writ,
order or direction in the nature of mandamus, and be pleased to hold and declare that the Petitioners are entitled to receive the amount of compensation as per award and be further direct the respondents to make the payment of the compensation to the Petitioners as per award under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.
(B) Your Lordship may be pleased to pass the any necessary order or direction to the respondent authorities to complete the procedure of releasing payment of compensation at the earliest or within some time bound schedule as the award is of 2015."
[4] The said writ petition was disposed of vide judgment and order dated 09.03.2023, a copy of which is appended at page '47' of the paper-book.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
While allowing the said writ petition directing to disburse the amount of compensation in favour of the petitioners after proper verification, it is noted by this Court that on the presentation of the said writ petition, by order dated 21.10.2020,
NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/435/2024 ORDER DATED: 09/12/2024 undefined this Court has directed the State authorities to deposit the amount under award of the land in question with the Registry of this Court on or before 27.11.2020.
It is also noted therein that the compensation amount, as per the directions of this Court, was deposited in the Registry on 10.11.2020.

In the judgment and order dated 09.03.2023, it was further recorded by this Court that the petitioners have been deprived of the fruits of the acquisition proceedings, inasmuch as, though award was Prashant Udayan Chinubhai vs Presiding Officer (Lara) on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172343172/
2 passed way back in the year 2015, but the compensation amount came to be deposited only on 10.11.2020 under the direction of this Court.

entities.text: Prashant Udayan Chinubhai vs Presiding Officer (Lara)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is, thus, evident that the compensation amount was disbursed to the petitioners / land owners only after the judgment and order dated 09.03.2023 passed by this Court.

[5] Further, there is nothing in the affidavit filed on behalf of the State authorities as to what had happened after 02.05.2015 and why on 10.07.2019, for the first time intimation was sent with regard to the making of the award to the petitioners.

The entire affidavit is silent about four years'
time taken by the State authorities in intimating the petitioners about the award dated 02.05.2015.

Further, we may note that after the notice was given NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/435/2024 ORDER DATED: 09/12/2024 undefined to the petitioners on 10.07.2019 and 09.10.2019 inspite of the application moved by him on 19.12.2019, compenssation was not disbursed.

In the meantime,
the country had faced with the unprecedented crisis of onset of COVID-19 and there was a nationwide lockdown effective from 23.03.2020.
The said situation with the continued lockdown came to an end only on 28.02.2022.
The Hon'ble Apex Court in Suo Moto Writ Petition (C) No.3 of 2020 has extended the statutory limitation period for the remedies available to the people across the Nation.

entities.text: Suo Moto Writ Petition (C) No.3 of 2020
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: [6] The period of approximately two years which remained disturbed due to onset of COVID-19 is required to be excluded, in the instant case, while computing the statutory limitation for making of the application under Section 64 of the Act, 2013.

Moreover, the petitioners have been denied fruits of compensation for about 5 years which was paid to them only after the disposal of the previous writ petition vide judgment and order dated 09.03.2023.

The petitioners who have not received compensation, cannot be said to be at fault in submitting the application seeking for making reference under Section 64 of the Act, 2013 after the NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/435/2024 ORDER DATED: 09/12/2024 undefined decision of the writ court.
The application moved by the petitioners dated 09.09.2023 under Section 64 of the Act, 2013, therefore, cannot be rejected on the ground of delay.

[7] To add to the above, it may be noted that there is an inordinate unexplained delay on the part of the State authorities in intimating the petitioners about making of the award dated 02.05.2015 and for the turn of events occurred after 10.07.2019, when the notice of the award for the first time was sent to the petitioners, the weight on the balance of equity lies in favour of the petitioners.

[8] With the above, while quashing the order dated 10.10.2023 passed by the Special Land Acquisition Officer, Ahmedabad, we revive the application dated 09.09.2023 filed by the petitioners under Section 64 of the Act, 2013.

The writ petition is accordingly, disposed of with the directions to the respondent No.2 herein to make a reference to the competent authority under Section 64 of the Act, 2013, to decide the same on the merits of the claim of the petitioners.

We may further make it clear that in view of the findings recorded by us hereinabove, it is incumbent upon the NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/435/2024 ORDER DATED: 09/12/2024 undefined competent authority,
namely, the Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Authority established under Section 51 of the Act, 2013 to decide the reference on its merits, as expeditiously as possible.
